name: @kitchensink/ingredient-parser
//runtime: This is the repository's FIRST non-Node deployable: a zip-packaged PYTHON Lambda running the
ingredient-parser-nlp CRF engine. The TypeScript here is its CDK stack, its packaging guard and the
zod its callers parse its response with -- never its runtime. See
//recipe-import-core: @kitchensink/recipe-import-core is TYPE-ONLY, and a devDependency on purpose (plan U22). This
package's parsed row and cookbook-import's JSONL row are the SAME six fields in two different
envelopes, and CrfReading is the shared row U22's promotion layer reads. The assertion that this
zod still satisfies it lives beside the zod (src/__tests__/engine.schema.test.ts) rather than in
the shared package, because a shared library must never import a service's. Nothing in this
package's deployed asset is TypeScript, so nothing here reaches the Lambda.
-- A comment key must sit at the TOP LEVEL, never inside dependencies/devDependencies: turbo
refuses to parse a non-string value there ('Incorrect type, expected a string, but received an
array'), which takes down every turbo-driven guard in packages/infra/global.

scripts.infra:synth: npm run bundle:lambda && cdk synth --app 'npx tsx infra/bin/app.ts'
scripts.infra:deploy: npm run bundle:lambda && cdk deploy --app 'npx tsx infra/bin/app.ts'

localSandbox.skipSynth: its `infra:synth` runs `bundle:lambda` first, which shells out to `python3 -m pip` for ~90 MB of arm64 wheels plus the 1.6 MB CRF model (ADR-0025). A local sandbox must not require a Python toolchain or network to START, and this stack contributes nothing a local run stands up: `awsResources.ts` creates no `AWS::Lambda::Function`, and `localCrfEngine.ts` runs `src/handler.py` directly. Set LOCAL_SANDBOX_SYNTH_ALL=1 to include it.
